In Coyoacán, it is a pleasure to leave a busy city street behind, head for a square and continue exploring Mexico City on foot. Historic houses, shady trees and small cafés make inviting places to stop. Hidalgo Square and Jardín Centenario stand side by side in the heart of the neighborhood. They are convenient starting points for a walk and for deciding where to go next.

The neighborhood is known for its cultural life and museums. Yet many of its pleasures lie between visits: admiring the doorway of an old house, browsing a market or finding a table in the shade. It is worth leaving time for little detours, since the next street may offer an entirely new scene.

Coyoacán will appeal to travelers who enjoy discovering a city through walks and everyday life. You can combine a museum visit with lunch, stroll around the central squares or linger by the craft stalls. Plan ahead for a particular museum, but leave some unstructured time to get to know the neighborhood. That way, your memories of Coyoacán will include both its cultural landmarks and a conversation over coffee.

Crystal Sound lies off the western side of the Antarctic Peninsula, near the Antarctic Circle. This stretch of sea has islands, drifting ice and views of the snow-covered coastline.

Expedition routes travel south into these waters along the Argentine Islands. For passengers, this stretch offers iceberg watching and the possibility of crossing the Antarctic Circle. Ice and weather conditions determine how far the vessel can travel and which activities are possible.

Cuernavaca's cathedral complex preserves the legacy of a 16th-century Franciscan monastery. Walking through its grounds reveals early religious architecture in Morelos, from the open atrium to the former monastery church.

Nearby chapels have distinctive decorative features, including the carved portal of the Chapel of the Third Order. The complex forms part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Earliest 16th-Century Monasteries on the Slopes of Popocatepetl." It is easy to combine a visit with the Palace of Cortés and explore Cuernavaca's religious and secular history on a single walk.
